venue: Family Dog at The Great Highway

ai_show_review.summary: Hard To Handle opener, tight China>Rider, but sagging Midnight Hour
ai_show_review.blurb: The set opens with a punchy Hard To Handle and flows into a seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider. Garcia delivers standout vocals on Black Peter and adds a tribal‑funk solo after In The Midnight Hour, though that song loses momentum. Overall the performance is uneven but packed with classic moments.
ai_show_review.review: On February 4, 1970 at the Family Dog on the Great Highway, the Dead delivered a mixed but memorable set. They kicked off with a rousing Hard To Handle before slipping into an exploratory China Cat Sunflower that segued flawlessly into I Know You Rider – a highlight that showcases their tight transitions. Garcia’s voice shines on Black Peter, delivering what reviewers called “top delivery,” and his post‑Midnight solo drifts into gliding tribal funk. Phil Lesh anchors the groove with a Santana‑style percussion feel during the jam after Midnight Hour, yet that very song stalls the momentum, leaving the set’s flow uneven. The remainder of the set—Cold Rain And Snow, Me & My Uncle, Saint Stephen, Not Fade Away—holds its own but never recaptures the early spark. Despite audio hiss and occasional drop‑outs on the full‑show recording, it remains the only source that captures the entire performance, making it essential listening for fans interested in this transitional era of the Dead’s evolution.

best_recording.reason: Only recording that captures the complete set; despite fair sound quality it provides the full performance.

key_highlights: Hard To Handle opens the show with high energy.
Seamless segue from China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider.
Garcia’s vocal peak on Black Peter and his tribal‑funk solo after Midnight Hour.
In The Midnight Hour drags, causing a dip in momentum.
